args.title: First win sets best time
args.description: With no stored best, a standard win becomes the best time.
args.given_when_then: Given no best time stored for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty

kwargs.interface_contract:
- Action `record_win`: params [`game_id`, `difficulty_id`, `elapsed_seconds`, `achieved_at`] — Applied automatically when a game is Won. For a standard difficulty (beginner, intermediate, expert) where elapsed_seconds < best_seconds, best_seconds becomes elapsed_seconds and game_id and achieved_at are updated; a slower or equal time keeps the stored best. A custom difficulty, or a difficulty_id differing from this record's, changes nothing.
- A newly created `BestTime` (constructed with only its required fields) holds: Constructed with id, difficulty_id (beginner, intermediate or expert), game_id, best_seconds and achieved_at from the first win of that difficulty; it holds exactly those values, with events empty.
- Field `difficulty_id` holds exactly one of: "beginner" (Best time for Beginner); "intermediate" (Best time for Intermediate); "expert" (Best time for Expert)
kwargs.other_rules:
- New best time: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds with T < B Then the best time becomes T for that difficulty on this device
- Slower or equal win keeps best: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins in T seconds with T >= B Then the best time remains B
- Custom games record no best time: Given a game on Custom difficulty When the player wins it Then no best time is created or changed
- Lost or abandoned games record no best time: Given a game that ends Lost or Abandoned When it ends Then no best time is created or changed

output:
import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


# "No best time stored" for a difficulty means no BestTime record exists yet.
# The first standard win creates one, with values taken from that win.
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at",
    [
        ("beginner", "game-b-1", 42, "2024-03-01T10:15:00Z"),
        ("intermediate", "game-i-1", 137, "2024-03-02T11:20:00Z"),
        ("expert", "game-e-1", 389, "2024-03-03T12:25:00Z"),
    ],
)
def test_first_win_sets_best_time(difficulty_id, game_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at):
    # Given no best time stored for this standard difficulty
    # When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds
    best = BestTime(
        id=f"best-{difficulty_id}",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id=game_id,
        best_seconds=elapsed_seconds,
        achieved_at=achieved_at,
    )

    # Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty.
    # The record was created from the first win only. There is no earlier best to compare against.
    # The "slower or equal" rule and the "new best" rule therefore do not apply.
    # The difficulty is standard and the game was won, so the custom rule and the
    # lost/abandoned rule do not apply either.
    # Expected: best_seconds == T.
    assert best.best_seconds == elapsed_seconds

    # The best time belongs to exactly the difficulty that was won.
    assert best.difficulty_id == difficulty_id

    # The winning game is the one credited with the best time.
    assert best.game_id == game_id

    # The moment of the winning game is recorded unchanged.
    assert best.achieved_at == achieved_at

    # The identifier passed at creation is kept.
    assert best.id == f"best-{difficulty_id}"

    # A newly created BestTime starts with no events.
    assert best.events == []
